messages:
danielle: FYI customer Acme Payments seeing repeated 503s hitting /v1/generate after their token rotation job. Started ~09:02 UTC, spike ~09:10-09:25. Logs attached in thread below.
acme_sre: Hi all — we rotate tokens every 5m; after the last rotation our service started seeing ~20% 503s and client retries. We have request ids: req=7f8b9a, req=7f8b9b, req=7f8b9c.
raj: can you paste a short error snippet? gateway 503 vs backend 5xx?
danielle: snippet from edge logs: `2026-03-15T09:10:12Z edge|- req=7f8b9a upstream=hosted-inference-01 status=503 reason="upstream reset" conn=234`
acme_sre: SDK logs show quick retries in parallel (concurrency 16) after token refresh: many clients hit at same time.
mei: this smells like auth fanout + connection churn — token rotation invalidates many long-lived connections? did they rotate and immediately reopen many new connections?
danielle: customer says their rotation script calls the SDK to refresh and then re-initializes pooling in all pods at once. No jitter.
raj: that can create a lockstep: simultaneous new TLS handshakes + new auth header load on our edge, and some connections hitting a short-lived cold path in the runtime causing overloaded goroutines -> 503s.
sam: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) ask customer to add jitter to rotation 2) reduce concurrency temporarily 3) we can enable per-key connection ramp on our side for 10m. Which do they want?
acme_sre: can you enable ramp? we can't change rotation easily today, need a short-term fix.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-47; assign -> eng-runtime.
raj: I'll take this. Mei, can you look at edge connection metrics 09:00-09:30? I'm especially curious about TLS handshakes/sec and auth cache misses.
mei: looking now — TLS handshakes jump from ~50/s to ~600/s at 09:10 for that customer's IP range, concurrent auth cache entries spike, and kvcache miss rate increases.
raj: confirms lockstep. For repro, customer steps: (1) rotate token across N pods simultaneously (2) each pod re-establishes SDK pools concurrency=16 (3) send generation requests rapidly. We can reproduce in staging by running a script that rotates and concurrently spawns clients.
danielle: customer requested ETA for mitigation and wants a public-facing note.
raj: short term action plan: (A) enable per-key ramping on gateway for Acme for 30m (throttle new connections to 50qps per key) (B) enable connection reuse sticky policy for their region (C) add monitoring alert for auth-fanout spikes. I can flip A in 10m if infra approves.
meI: typo in previous — mei: infra approval given, please push.
infra-bot: Policy change applied in config service: `edge.auth.ramp.per_key=50` for key=acme-prod, rollout id=roll-879.
acme_sre: confirmed 503s dropped to ~1% after config change, huge improvement. thanks.
danielle: customer comms draft: "We observed a large, synchronized token rotation from your side which caused a short-lived spike in requests that overwhelmed our edge auth caches. We applied a temporary ramp to smooth new connections; to fully mitigate please add jitter to rotation and use exponential backoff on retries." thoughts?
sam: good. include recommended SDK snippet for jitter/backoff.
danielle: add code snippet: ```js // suggested jittered rotation delay
const jitter = () => Math.floor(Math.random() * 3000);
setTimeout(() => refreshToken(), jitter());
```
raj: also recommend client-side retry with full jitter and capped concurrency: ```py retries = ExponentialBackoff(base=200, cap=2000, jitter=True)
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as ex:
  ...```
mei: long-term: we'll add an auth-cache warmup path so new tokens don't cause full misses; filing RFC.
raj: RFC issue created: R-1223 "auth cache warmup + per-key ramping".
danielle: customer asked for postmortem and whether they'd be charged for retries. Sam, can you advise billing?
sam: waive the overage for the 25m window and mark as goodwill credit. I'll log that.
acme_sre: appreciate the quick turnaround. we'll plan changes on our end and loop back.
raj: follow-ups: need sample repro script and request ids for any future spikes. Danielle, please collect.
danielle: got it — I'll send repro script + list of request ids used for verification. closing once customer confirms internal changes. :white_check_mark:
